Company Overview Meridian Fabrication Co. was founded in 2011 by a small group of mechanical and software engineers with a shared interest in building precision manufacturing equipment for the renewable energy sector. What began as a ten-person workshop in a converted warehouse has since grown into a company of over four hundred employees across three sites, with headquarters remaining at our original location. Our mission is to design and build fabrication systems that make sustainable manufacturing accessible to smaller producers who would otherwise be priced out of automation. This handbook describes the policies, benefits, and expectations that apply to all Meridian employees. It is reviewed annually by People Operations and Legal, and employees are notified by email whenever a material change is made. Meridian's culture is built around three principles: craftsmanship, accountability, and mutual trust. We expect every employee to take ownership of their work, communicate openly about setbacks, and treat colleagues with the same care they would want extended to themselves. These principles inform how we approach everything from performance management to time off, and they are referenced throughout this handbook. 2. Compensation & Pay Structure Meridian pays all employees on a semi-monthly basis, on the 15th and last business day of each month. Base salaries are set according to leveled pay bands that are reviewed annually against external market data. All full-time employees in good standing are eligible for the annual performance bonus, paid each March, equal to up to 10% of base salary depending on individual and company performance that year. Bonus percentages are communicated individually and are not guaranteed to be uniform across teams. Part-time and contract employees are not eligible for the annual bonus program under any circumstances. Annual merit increases, where applicable, are effective each July and are communicated alongside the employee's midyear check-in. Merit increases and the annual bonus are evaluated separately and one does not guarantee the other. 3. Time Off Policies 3.1 Flexible Time Off (FTO) Full-time employees hired on or after January 2019 accrue Flexible Time Off (FTO) rather than traditional PTO. FTO is accrued at a rate of 1.5 days per month, totaling 18 days annually for a full-time employee, and may be used for vacation, personal matters, or short-term illness of less than three consecutive days. FTO does not roll over between calendar years, and unused balances are not paid out upon departure except where required by local law. 3.2 Legacy PTO Plan Employees hired before January 2019 remain on the legacy Paid Time Off (PTO) plan unless they have voluntarily opted into FTO in writing. Extended Sick Leave provides up to 10 paid days per calendar year and may require a physician's note for absences longer than five consecutive days. Bereavement leave for an extended family member (grandparent, aunt, uncle, or in-law) is capped at 2 paid days. Additional circumstances affecting bereavement leave duration are described in Section 9 of this handbook. 3.5 Parental Leave Meridian provides 12 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 4 weeks for the secondary caregiver, regardless of the employee's time-off plan. Benefits Meridian offers medical, dental, and vision coverage to all full-time employees, effective on the first day of the month following hire. The company covers 80% of the premium for employee-only coverage and 60% of the premium for dependent coverage. Meridian matches 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to 4% of an employee's base salary. Matching contributions vest immediately and are deposited each pay period alongside the employee's own contribution. All employees and their household members have access to the company's EAP, which provides confidential counseling sessions, financial planning consultations, and legal referrals at no cost. The EAP can be reached 24 hours a day through the number listed on the internal benefits portal, and usage is never reported to managers or People Operations in identifiable form. 5. Remote Work Policy Meridian supports a flexible approach to remote work, recognizing that a distributed, trust-based culture improves both morale and output while maintaining the collaborative spirit that has defined our engineering teams since the company's founding. Remote and hybrid employees are expected to maintain core collaboration hours between 10am and 3pm in their assigned time zone, and to remain reachable via company messaging tools during standard business hours. to maintain core collaboration hours between 10am and 3pm in their assigned time zone, and to remain reachable via company messaging tools during standard business hours. Managers are encouraged to set team-level norms that go beyond this minimum where collaboration needs require it, and teams that work across more than two time zones are encouraged to document their agreed-upon overlap hours in their team charter. Employees who wish to work temporarily from outside their home country for personal travel may do so for up to 20 consecutive days per calendar year without triggering additional tax residency documentation; extended stays beyond this threshold require prior written approval from both People Operations and Legal before travel begins, and failure to obtain approval may result in the employee bearing personal responsibility for any resulting tax liability. 6. Expense Reimbursement 6.1 General Limits Employees may claim reimbursement for reasonable business expenses, including client meals, local transportation, and approved software subscriptions. Client meal expenses up to $150 per event do not require pre-approval; amounts exceeding $150 require written approval from a manager prior to the expense being incurred. Expenses exceeding $2,000 in total are escalated to the Expense Review Committee, which meets on the first Monday of each month to evaluate larger requests. 6.2 Submission Deadlines All expense reports, regardless of category, must be submitted through the Expense Portal within 30 days of the expense date. Reports submitted after this window will not be reimbursed except in cases of documented travel delays or system outages affecting the Expense Portal itself. 7. Performance Management Formal performance reviews occur annually each October, with informal check-ins recommended on a quarterly basis between employees and their managers. Review outcomes feed into the following July's merit increase cycle described in Section 2. Employees whose performance falls below expectations may be placed on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) by their manager, in consultation with People Operations. A PIP typically runs for 60 to 90 days and includes specific, measurable goals. Employees on an active PIP are not eligible for the annual performance bonus described in Section 2, nor for consideration in the mid-year promotion cycle, until the PIP has been successfully closed by their manager. 8. New Hire Orientation & Company Resources During their first week, new hires meet with People Operations to review benefits enrollment, complete required compliance training, and are introduced to available support resources, including the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) confidential counseling line and the internal mentorship program, which pairs new hires with a peer outside their immediate team for their first six months. 9.
